evidence: Filtering by API module shows only the 5 API-labeled documents; selecting All restores the full 19-item list.

Document detail for rest-api-design shows title, description, version v2.3.0, update date 2024-01-15, content sections (REST Principles, Endpoint Naming Conventions, Pagination & Filtering), and related documents list (4 items).

Collapsing rest-principles section removed its body paragraph text; its reference links remain visible but become disabled ('Expand section to access link'); the section header remains clickable to reopen.
Re-expanding rest-principles restored the content paragraph and both reference links (api-versioning, error-handling) as enabled navigation targets.
Each section toggle exposes a state field (open/closed) that matches visibility: rest-principles shows 'open' with content+links visible; endpoint-naming/pagination show 'closed' with content hidden.

Clicking link in collapsed endpoint-naming section showed toast 'Please expand the section to access links' and kept document at REST API Design Guidelines. After expanding, clicking the same link navigated to HTTP Methods Guide.
Clicking the HTTP Methods Guide reference link (in an expanded section) navigated the document view to that document (doc.title became 'HTTP Methods Guide').

Checked rest-api-design (related: api-versioning, error-handling, http-methods, rate-limiting; section links: api-versioning, error-handling, http-methods) and http-methods (related/section link: rest-api-design only) — neither lists itself.
Searching 'zzzznonexistentquery' shows 'No documents found - Try adjusting your search or filter criteria'; clearing the search restores all 19 documents.

issue: Favorites view does not expose every favorited document when a Documents module filter is active
actual: Favorited rest-api-design (API) and jwt-authentication (AUTH). With Documents module filter set to 'API', switching to Favorites view (count correctly showed 2) only rendered rest-api-design item; jwt-authentication was missing from the DOM. Resetting the Documents filter to 'All' then made both favorites appear in the Favorites view. Favorite markers themselves did survive filtering/sorting within Documents (rest-api-design stayed 'on' after API filter + date sort), and the nav badge count updated immediately (1 then 2) on toggling — but the Favorites view visibility bug means the requirement 'Favorites view continues to expose every favorited document regardless of a module filter used in Documents' fails.

evidence: Graph renders exactly 19 nodes (matching the 19 documents), each node circle stroke color varies by module (distinct colors observed for API, AUTH, DATA, UI, CORE), and a line edge exists connecting rest-api-design and http-methods coordinates matching their known related-document relationship.
graph.nodes collection lists all 19 documents across modules; zoom-in/zoom-out/reset-view controls are present to bring the full graph into view.
Clicking database-schema node set its state to 'selected'. Zoom In changed graph.zoom from 100% to 120%; Reset View returned it to 100%.

issue: Clicking a knowledge-graph node does not open the document view
actual: Clicking a graph node (e.g. database-schema, then session-management) only toggles its 'selected' visual state; the Knowledge Graph tab remains active and no navigation to the document view occurs. Verified with single click, repeated click on the same already-selected node, dblclick, and Enter key while focused — none triggered navigation to document.detail despite the node's semantic hint declaring target='document.detail'.

evidence: Set document to Session Management with session-storage collapsed and session-security expanded, set graph zoom to 140%. After switching Graph→Favorites→Graph, zoom remained 140%. After switching Graph→Documents, document remained Session Management with identical section expand/collapse states.
Three navigation tabs (Documents, Knowledge Graph, Favorites) are present; each becomes 'active' when clicked and successfully switched among all three throughout testing.

issue: Clicking a knowledge-graph node does not switch to the document view
actual: Clicking a graph node (e.g. database-schema, then session-management) updates the node's 'selected' visual state and silently changes the underlying current-document state (confirmed: after manually switching to the Documents tab afterward, the last-clicked node's document was shown), but the app does NOT automatically switch the active tab to Documents/document view as required by 'without requiring a separate tab change'. The user remains on the Knowledge Graph tab after clicking a node and must manually click the Documents tab to see the opened document.
